title: Responsible adoption of AI in health
blurb: AI is often evaluated on its own, apart from the situations, relationships, and information systems it enters. I study what these systems produce and assess it in context, so that both the public and the clinicians they serve can judge when a tool belongs in health.

title: How people perceive and trust AI
blurb: How people act on AI depends less on what it can do than on what they take it to be. I pair analysis of public discourse over time with controlled experiments to trace how AI is represented, and how that shapes the trust and roles people assign it.

title: Health signals and support in everyday life
blurb: Formal healthcare systems overlook much of what social and everyday data reveal, and much of the care that happens beyond their reach. I study both what these spaces disclose about health and the support people find within them.
